dedupe_keys.name: rescult european interoperable database for cultural heritage resilience

description: The ResCult European Interoperable Database is the spatial database of the ResCult project, Increasing Resilience of Cultural heritage, which aimed to help civil protection bodies prevent and mitigate disaster impacts on cultural heritage sites. It was built by Elisabetta Colucci, Francesca Matrone and colleagues at Politecnico di Torino with TU Delft and the LINKS Foundation as an integrated database for civil protection, national cultural heritage ministries, the European Union and local authorities, designed around 3D GIS, the INSPIRE geographic standards and interoperability, in support of risk and vulnerability analysis and a Sendai-aligned disaster risk reduction strategy. Coverage: European cultural heritage assets, as far as they were loaded in the project. Access: one PostgreSQL backup file of about 2.4 GB on Zenodo (version of 30 October 2020, published 2021-11-10) and the project website. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: the record does not list which sites or hazards are populated, and restoring it needs a PostgreSQL server; the project has ended. Simulation uses are a structured inventory of heritage buildings for hazard exposure and vulnerability studies and a schema reference for civil protection data on protected buildings. Related records: the cultural heritage point cloud segmentation record.
